abort.already_configured: The add-on's Voice PE is set up already: the add-on serves one device.
abort.other_addon: Another add-on offered a link to the Voice PE: only the add-on the integration was set up with can change it. If you moved to a new copy of the add-on, remove this integration and add it again.
abort.invalid_offer: The add-on's offer isn't in a form the Voice PE takes: a port, a secret of 16 to 128 visible characters, a certificate, and a fingerprint key.
abort.link_updated: The Voice PE takes the add-on's new link.

user.title: The add-on's Voice PE
user.description: Pick the Voice PE that runs the add-on's firmware. It becomes an Assist satellite, so Home Assistant's announce and start conversation actions reach the OpenAI assistant on it.

discovery_pick.title: The add-on's Voice PE
discovery_pick.description:
Pick the Voice PE that runs the add-on's firmware. It becomes an Assist satellite, so Home Assistant's announce and start conversation actions reach the OpenAI assistant on it.

This also links the Voice PE to the add-on that made the offer:

- Add-on: `{slug}`
- Link fingerprint: `{fingerprint}`

The add-on's log shows its link's fingerprint at every start: set this up only if they match.

discovery_confirm.title: The add-on's Voice PE
discovery_confirm.description:
Set up {name}, the Voice PE that runs the add-on's firmware, as an Assist satellite? Home Assistant's announce and start conversation actions will then reach the OpenAI assistant on it.

This also links the Voice PE to the add-on that made the offer:

- Add-on: `{slug}`
- Link fingerprint: `{fingerprint}`

The add-on's log shows its link's fingerprint at every start: set this up only if they match.

confirm_link.title: A new link to the add-on
confirm_link.description:
An add-on offers {name} a new link: its secret, certificate or port changed.

- Add-on: `{slug}`
- Link fingerprint: `{fingerprint}`

The add-on's log shows its link's fingerprint at every start. Confirm only if it matches and you changed the add-on: the Voice PE then connects with the new link.

init.title: The add-on's address
init.description: Where the Voice PE finds the add-on. Leave empty for Home Assistant's own address on your network, which suits the add-on running on Home Assistant's host; set it if the device needs another, such as a name it resolves. It starts with wss:// and has the add-on's port, such as wss://192.0.2.10:8080/.

error.not_wss: The address must start with wss://: the add-on only takes encrypted connections.

press_button.title: Press the centre button on {name}
press_button.description: {name} is ready to link to the add-on, and waits for its centre button before it takes the link: its lights twinkle warm white. Press the button once. Pressing it is how the device knows someone at it agreed to the link.

other_link_waiting.title: Don't press the centre button on {name}
other_link_waiting.description: {name} is waiting for its centre button to accept a link that isn't this add-on's: something else in Home Assistant set it. Don't press the button. Restart the device (unplug it and plug it back in) to clear that link; it then gets the add-on's, and asks for the press here.

linked_elsewhere.title: Reset {name} now
linked_elsewhere.description:
{name} holds a link to an add-on that this integration didn't give it, and refuses the integration's. Until you reset it, it may be sending what its microphone hears somewhere other than your add-on.

Reset it now: hold its centre button down past the first warning, until its lights turn solid red (about 22 seconds), then let go. That erases its link, its Wi-Fi and its encryption key. Then give it your Wi-Fi again, add it to Home Assistant again, and press its centre button only when Home Assistant asks you to here.

If you build its firmware yourself with a link in it, build it again with the add-on's device secret instead.
